Zaid b. Haritha was called son of Muhammad until a verse said to name people after their fathers; the Prophet defended Usama's and Zaid's command, both among his dearest.
Abdullah b. Ja'far recalled the Prophet mounting him and Fatima's sons on his beast on returning from journeys, and telling him a secret he would tell no one.
The Prophet said the best women of their time were Mary and Khadija, the perfect women Mary and Asiya, and that Aisha excels women as tharid excels other foods.
Khadija got her Lord's greeting through Gabriel and news of a jewelled palace in Paradise; Aisha was jealous as the Prophet praised her and sent meat to her friends.
The Prophet dreamt of Aisha brought in silk, knew her moods by her oaths, let her play with dolls, and told Fatima, sent by his wives, that he loved Aisha.
In his last illness the Prophet awaited Aisha's turn and died against her chest, asking pardon and mercy and choosing the highest companions, as every prophet is given a choice.
Aisha, jealous when Hafsa swapped camels, excels women like tharid among foods; Gabriel greeted her, and the Prophet said he was to her as Abu Zar' to Umm Zar'.
The Prophet said Fatima is part of him, objecting to Ali also marrying Abu Jahl's daughter, and in his last illness secretly told her of his death and her rank.
Umm Salama took Gabriel, talking with the Prophet, for Dihya; the Prophet said the longest-handed wife would join him first, and it was Zainab, who worked and gave in charity.
The Prophet visited Umm Aiman, who was annoyed when he declined her drink; after his death Abu Bakr and Umar visited her and wept with her that revelation had ceased.
The Prophet visited Umm Sulaim, whose brother was killed with him; he heard her and Bilal's steps in Paradise and blessed her and Abu Talha after their son's death.
The Prophet counted Ibn Mas'ud among the believers of verse 5:93; Abu Musa took him for one of the Prophet's household, and Abu Mas'ud knew no one left more learned.
Ibn Mas'ud recited seventy-plus surahs before the Prophet, who named him, Salim, Ubayy and Mu'adh as Quran teachers; four Ansar collected it, and Allah ordered it recited to Ubayy.
The Prophet said the Throne of the Most Compassionate shook at Sa'd b. Mu'adh's death, and that his kerchiefs in Paradise were better than a silk garment people admired.
At Uhud the Prophet offered his sword to one who would fulfil its right; Abu Dujana took it and struck the heads of the polytheists.
The Prophet said angels shaded Jabir's mutilated father, killed at Uhud, as his relatives wept, and he lifted Julaibib, killed after killing seven, in his arms for burial.
Abu Dharr came to Mecca to find the Prophet, lived on Zamzam water, embraced Islam, proclaimed it aloud and was beaten, and half of his tribe Ghifar then accepted Islam.
Since Jarir embraced Islam the Prophet never refused to see him and always smiled at him, and prayed that he be firm on horseback and rightly guided.
At the Prophet's request Jarir led Ahmas horsemen against Dhu'l-Khalasah, an idol-house called the Yamanite Ka'ba, and destroyed and burned it, and the Prophet blessed Ahmas's horses and men.
Ibn Abbas placed water for the Prophet's ablution, and the Prophet prayed that Allah grant him deep understanding of religion.
Ibn Umar dreamt a silk cloth flew wherever he aimed in Paradise and angels took him to the Fire; the Prophet called him pious and wished he prayed at night.
Umm Sulaim brought Anas to serve the Prophet, who prayed for increase in his wealth and children, and Anas kept a secret the Prophet told him, even from his mother.
The Prophet said Abdullah b. Salam was in Paradise and explained his dream of climbing a pillar to a handhold as holding fast to Islam until death.
The Prophet had Hassan b. Thabit answer the Quraysh's satire for him, with Gabriel's help, and Aisha told a man scolding Hassan to leave him, as he defended the Prophet.
After the Prophet prayed, Abu Huraira's mother accepted Islam; Abu Huraira says he narrates much because he stayed with the Prophet and never forgot, and Aisha faulted his hasty narrating.
Hatib's letter to the Meccans was seized; the Prophet accepted his explanation, refused Umar's wish to kill him as he fought at Badr, and said he would not enter Hell.
The Prophet said none who pledged allegiance under the Tree would enter Hell, and answered Hafsa's objection with the verse that Allah rescues the God-conscious and leaves the tyrants there.
The Prophet gave Abu Musa and Bilal glad tidings a Bedouin refused, prayed forgiveness for Abu Amir and Abu Musa, and praised the Ash'arites' night recitation and food-sharing.
Abu Sufyan asked the Prophet to marry his daughter Umm Habiba, take Mu'awiya as scribe and make him a commander against the unbelievers, and the Prophet agreed to all three.
Asma bint Umais told the Prophet Umar claimed more right to him for emigrating first; he said the people of the boat, back from Abyssinia, had two emigrations, Umar one.
When Abu Bakr rebuked Salman, Suhaib and Bilal for their words about Abu Sufyan, the Prophet said annoying them would annoy his Lord, and Abu Bakr apologised to them.
A verse came down about two Ansar clans, the Prophet prayed for forgiveness for the Ansar and their offspring, and said they were dearest to him and his trusted ones.
The Prophet ranked the best Ansar clans, with good in all; Sa'd b. Ubada was upset his clan came fourth, and Jarir served Anas as the Ansar served the Prophet.
The Prophet said Allah pardoned the tribe of Ghifar and kept Aslam safe, and in prayer cursed Lihyan, Ri'l, Dhakwan and Usayya for disobeying Allah and His Messenger.
The Prophet called the Ansar, Quraysh, Muzaina, Juhaina, Ghifar and Ashja' his friends, and said Aslam, Ghifar, Muzaina and Juhaina are better than Tamim, Amir, Asad and Ghatafan.
Tayyi's alms gladdened the Prophet, he prayed for Daws to be guided rather than cursed, and Abu Huraira heard him call Banu Tamim the bravest in battle.
The Prophet said those good before Islam are good in Islam if they understand it, the best shun authority until it is thrust on them, and the worst are double-faced.
The Prophet said the best camel-riding women are those of Quraysh, kind to children when small and careful of a husband's wealth; he said it when proposing to Umm Hani.
The Prophet established brotherhood between the Quraysh and the Ansar in his house, and said Islam has no alliances except those made for good before it, which it strengthens.
The Prophet said he safeguards his Companions and they his community, and armies will win having among them one who saw him, or saw those who saw him.
